newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-SMOOTH SAMPRAS SAUNTERS INTO THIRD ROUND.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SMOOTH SAMPRAS SAUNTERS INTO THIRD ROUND.

text.p: The claycourt dreams of Pete Sampras moved into sharper focus on Wednesday as the world number one reinforced his position among this year's leading French Open title contenders.

The American top seed, determined to do everything in his power to scoop the only Grand Slam title he has never won, looked highly impressive during a 6-1 6-2 6-2 demolition of Spain's Francisco Clavet in a contest viewed beforehand as a good test of Sampras's ambitions on clay.
Instead, the Spaniard was sunk without trace by some high-quality shot-making which suggested that any uncertainty Sampras used to experience at Roland Garros is no longer present.

"I feel pretty strong," said Sampras, who required only 87 minutes to complete a smooth job on centre court where he lost in last year's semifinal to Yevgeny Kafelnikov, a result he now admits came as a considerable blow.
"I had mixed emotions last year after I left because I had beaten very good clay court players like Sergi Bruguera but still I lost," recalled Sampras.

This year, however, he has returned with hunger renewed and has discovered that half of Paris are on his side too. "I feel the crowd know it is the one tournament I haven't won. They seem to be behind me."

Like Sampras, defending champion Kafelnikov has also yet to drop a set and are starting to concern those who predicted the tournament would be a simple showdown between a succession of Spanish clay specialists.

The Russian third seed beat France's Guillaume Raoux 7-5 6-3 6-4 in 94 minutes and, although he insists he is "not the same player" he was before his recent three-month injury lay-off, the Parisian clay appears to bring the best out of him.
He is now scheduled to meet France's Cedric Pioline, with both players well aware that Thomas Muster, below his best in recent months, is the only other remaining seed in their quarter.

On another dry, sunny day, Spain's Alex Corretja was a 4-6 6-1 6-1 7-6 winner against Germany's Jens Knippschild despite feeling less than 100 percent, while Steffi Graf reminded the women's field of her presence with a 6-3 6-3 win over last year's French junior champion Amelie Mauresmo of France.
The world number two remains on course for a quarter-final meeting with seventh seed Conchita Martinez who cruised past the flimsy challenge of American Chanda Rubin 6-3 6-0.
